response.title: A Safe Visit to Pine Creek
response.passage:
The environmental club planned to measure water clarity at Pine Creek. After rain flooded the path beside the creek, Ms. Wu moved the group’s meeting point to a raised platform. Before they left school, she checked the park office’s daily report. The report was reliable because park staff posted water levels before opening each morning. It warned that the current under the footbridge was unusually strong after the storm. The students packed clear jars and a measuring chart, but left their wading boots at school.

At the platform, a guide asked them to compare the creek with a photograph taken before the rain. Unlike the old picture, today’s surface carried small branches quickly toward the bend. This movement made the danger easy to notice, although the water near the bank looked shallow. They recorded the water’s color from above instead of entering the creek. Back at school, they used their notes to explain why testing water should never come before safety.
